subject: Clarify: what is stored by default for requests vs model outputs (SkyFin compliance ask)
messages:
From: Maya Patel <maya.patel@skyfin.ai>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Cc: DataOps Team <dataops@skyfin.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify: what Redwood keeps by default for user requests and outputs

Hi Stephanie,

Quick one from our compliance team as we finalize the integration runbook: can you confirm what Redwood stores by default when a user sends a prompt to the hosted API? Specifically:
- Are the raw user inputs (prompts) retained, and for how long?
- Are intermediate streamed tokens captured and persisted?
- How long are final generated outputs retained, and are they stored in raw form or hashed/derivative?
- Is KV-cache data or session state ever persisted beyond the session lifetime?

We're trying to map this to our internal data retention policy and to answer an upcoming SOC questionnaire. If you have a short summary PDF or an internal one-pager, that would help.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if easier.

— Maya
Senior PM, Integrations
SkyFin AI

Attachment: none

From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
To: Maya Patel <maya.patel@skyfin.ai>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify: what Redwood keeps by default for user requests and outputs

Maya — thanks for the clear list. TL;DR below and I'll attach a short summary.

- Raw prompts (user-submitted text): default store = 30 days for hosted customers; can be configured to 0 (no storage) via project settings for Enterprise/Private.
- Streamed tokens: captured transiently to support streaming clients but not archived by default; ephemeral window = 48 hours for debugging traces, then purged unless flagged by an incident.
- Final outputs: stored for 90 days by default to support quality/regression monitoring; we store the output text and associated metadata (model version, prompt hash). For customers with stricter needs we offer a no-retention mode and an export-only mode.
- KV-cache/session state: ephemeral by design; cached on the serving layer and evicted per session (TTL default 24 hours), not written to long-term stores.

I'm looping in Kimberly and Karthik to confirm the retention windows and to surface any contract-level exceptions. Attaching the one-pager I promised.

Next steps: if SkyFin needs shorter windows (e.g., 7 days) or explicit erasure SLA, we can propose a dedicated retention profile in the SOW.

— Stephanie
Director, Solutions 
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-retention-summary-2026.pdf

Kimberly / Karthik — forwarding SkyFin's questions. I drafted the TL;DR above. Can you confirm the legal/controls wording for the hosted plan? A few points we should double-check before I send the formal reply:
- Confirm default host retention windows (30d prompts, 90d outputs) and whether we classify final outputs as "derived artifacts" vs PII-sensitive content.
- Confirm that streamed-token traces are purged after 48h unless flagged.
- KV cache TTL default 24h and never persisted to object storage for hosted accounts.
- Provide the erasure request route (support vs. self-serve API) and expected SLA for hosted customers.

I added a copy of the retention one-pager.

— S

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 08:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Clarify: what Redwood keeps by default for user requests and outputs

Stephanie,

Thanks for the summary — I've reviewed and updated a couple of points for compliance precision. Please use the following language in your customer reply (we'll track this in the SOC artifact repo as well):

1) Default retention windows (hosted API, unless overridden in contract):
   - Customer input (raw prompt text): stored for 30 days from ingest. This includes any explicit prompt templates submitted as part of the request.
   - Streamed tokens / partial responses: short-term diagnostic traces are retained for up to 48 hours and then permanently deleted. These traces are captured solely to support streaming clients and debug real-time delivery; they are not used for model training.
   - Final generated output: retained for 90 days by default. Final outputs are stored in plaintext to enable deterministic replay and quality monitoring; we associate a cryptographic hash with each stored output for integrity checks.
   - KV-cache / session state: not persisted to long-term object stores for hosted customers. Session caches are stored in-memory on serving nodes with a default TTL of 24 hours; they are scrubbed on node recycle and do not survive deployment restarts.

2) Data residency: For hosted customers we store data in the region selected at project creation (US, EU, or APAC). Data exported for audits follows the same residency constraints unless otherwise requested in the contract.

3) Erasure and exports:
   - Self-serve project-level erasure: customers can opt to disable retention (set to "no retention") which prevents new requests from being written to long-term stores.
   - Support-assisted erasure: for historical data removal customers submit an erasure request (sample form attached). For hosted plans we target completion within 30 days of request; enterprise/private plans negotiate SLA in SOW.

4) Exceptions & notes:
   - In the event of a security incident, relevant traces may be retained longer for investigation with legal approval and customer notification.
   - Redaction: customers may configure automated PII redaction in-transit via our SDKs; this is recommended for high-sensitivity workloads.

Please confirm and then send to Maya with the one-pager attached. I've also added the SOC artifact link for their auditors.

— Kimberly (Security & Compliance)

Attachment: sample-erasure-request-form.docx
